title: Dynamic play: does the activity pay, or only look like it?
outcomes: Looks at both pawn structures and the lines before judging, and notices when neither side has damaged pawns
Judges whether the activity pays for the structure and states the verdict as practical (from his count)
Treats a verdict as engine-checked only when the engine's rating at the stated depth agrees
Does not say 'damaged structure means worse' without a count

steps.text: The lesson *Dynamic play: count the activity, not only the pawns* taught the two lists. Here nothing tells you what to count: either side may have damage, or neither. First the pawns, then the lines and pieces. Your verdict is **practical**: a judgement from your count. Only the engine's rating at its stated depth can make it **engine-checked**, and even that is evidence, not proof.

Activity pays only while it can be used. *Rule of thumb:* count the open files and the squares your most active piece attacks; if the lines are shut, the activity is on paper. A trade of your active pieces can turn the count. When neither side has an isolated, doubled or backward pawn, there is nothing to weigh against: judge the position by other means. Compare the three positions below.

steps.title: Paid for, not paid for, nothing to weigh
steps.prompt: Predict the answer in each position. In the first two, Black's knight stands on g6 in one and on h8 in the other. Name that one change, then say why the third position needs no count.

Paper exercise (the app does not check it): take a position from one of your games where a side had damaged pawns. Write your verdict first and label it *practical*. Then run the engine in My games and write what it rated; label it engine-checked only if the rating agrees.
